final.answer: Yes — per the datasheet for FV-104-2 (Fisher ET), the valve is available with flanged ends, not only buttweld or screwed. Flanged options include cast iron bodies with CL125 FF or CL250 RF flanges, steel bodies with RF or RTJ flanges in CL150/CL300/CL600, and EN flanges (EN1092-1/B, PN16–PN100) on raised-face steel bodies. Butt weld and socket weld are steel-body options, and screwed ends are only offered in NPS 1, 1-1/2 or 2. Exact availability depends on the valve variant, size and body material (Table 3, page 5).

final.answer: The valve operated by FIC-106-2 is FV-106-2. Its datasheet (Fisher ET, Table 14, p. 20) lists the following plug seal ring materials and temperature limits: 2-piece valve plug seal — carbon-filled PTFE (−73 to 232 °C / −100 to 450 °F), ethylene-propylene (−40 to 232 °C / −40 to 450 °F; not for petroleum-based fluids/hydrocarbons), fluorocarbon (−18 to 204 °C / 0 to 400 °F; not for steam or ammonia), and nitrile (−40 to 71 °C / −40 to 160 °F for air and hydrocarbons, −40 to 82 °C / −40 to 180 °F for other compatible fluids). Spring-loaded valve plug seal — PTFE with N10276 spring (−73 to 232 °C / −100 to 450 °F) and PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring (−73 to 316 °C / −100 to 600 °F, but only up to 260 °C / 500 °F in oxidizing service). Other ring materials (stainless steel seal ring parts, PEEK anti-extrusion rings, PTFE V-ring packing at −40 to 232 °C) are marked as not limiting for temperature. No part explicitly called a "piston ring" is named in the datasheet; the plug seal rings above are the closest items.

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [20, 21, 2]:
The valve plug seal (the seal ring in the plug) comes in several materials, each with its own temperature range — see Table 14, "Materials and Temperature Limits for Other Parts", on page 20 (with notes on page 21).

**2-piece valve plug seal** (standard for NPS 1 thru 6 valves except those with Cavitrol III cage) [p. 20]:
- Carbon-filled PTFE: −73 °C to 232 °C (−100 °F to 450 °F)
- Ethylene-propylene: −40 °C to 232 °C (−40 °F to 450 °F). Note: good with hot water/steam and most fire-resistant hydraulic oils, but cannot be used with petroleum-based fluids and other hydrocarbons.
- Fluorocarbon: −18 °C to 204 °C (0 °F to 400 °F). Note: for high-temperature air, hydrocarbons and certain other chemicals and solvents; not for steam or ammonia; not recommended for water above 82 °C / 180 °F.
- Nitrile (for air and hydrocarbons): −40 °C to 71 °C (−40 °F to 160 °F); for other compatible fluids: −40 °C to 82 °C (−40 °F to 180 °F). Note: cannot be used with fire-resistant hydraulic oils.

**Spring-loaded valve plug seal** (standard for NPS 8 valve regardless of cage and all NPS 1 thru 6 valves with Cavitrol III cages; optional in NPS 1 thru 6 valves with other cages) [p. 20]:
- PTFE with N10276 spring: −73 °C to 232 °C (−100 °F to 450 °F)

final.answer: The drawing does not identify which transmitter feeds FIC-10-2, so the specific tag cannot be confirmed. However, the transmitter datasheet (Rosemount 3051) states that on a detected sensor or microprocessor failure the output is driven either high or low — the direction is not fixed but user-selectable. For the HART 4-20 mA output, you change the alarm direction with a jumper/switch on the transmitter (or by ordering the 'Alarm levels' option: high alarm code C4, low alarm code CN, or custom levels CR/CS); default levels are high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA and low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA (NAMUR: ≥ 22.5 mA / ≤ 3.6 mA). For the 1-5 V low-power output, the direction is selected by an internal jumper (high alarm > 5.4 V, low alarm < 0.94 V). Digital outputs (Fieldbus etc.) have no high/low analog alarm direction — failure is passed as an alert/status. The factory standard configuration is alarm = High.

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [88, 26, 42, 63, 74, 15, 52, 85]:
On signal failure the transmitter can drive its output either high or low — the direction is not fixed, but is selected by you, using a jumper/switch on the transmitter (an internal jumper for the 1-5 V low-power output). [p. 88]

Details (all from page 88):

**HART 4-20 mA output (option code A):**
- If self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the analog signal is driven either high or low to alert the user.
- High or low failure mode is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter.
- The actual current levels depend on how the alarm levels are configured (see Table 5 on page 88, "Failure mode alarm"):
  - Default setting: high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA (footnote: high alarm default is ≥ 22.5 mA for some options — codes M6, DA1, T9, RK)
  - NAMUR-compliant setting (option codes C4 or CN): high alarm ≥ 22.5 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.6 mA
  - Custom levels: high alarm 20.2–23.0 mA, low alarm 3.6–3.8 mA (footnote: low alarm must be 0.1 mA less than low saturation, and high alarm must be 0.1 mA greater than high saturation)

**1-5 V low-power output (Output code M):**
- On a gross transmitter failure the signal is driven below 0.94 V (low alarm) or above 5.4 V (high alarm).
- High or low alarm signal is user-selectable by internal jumper.

**Digital outputs (codes F, W, X — e.g. FOUNDATION Fieldbus):** there is no high/low analog alarm direction; a gross failure is passed as an alert and a status along with the process variable. [p. 88]

Also worth knowing: when ordering, the alarm direction can be chosen via the "Alarm levels" option — high alarm (code C4), low alarm (code CN), or custom high/low levels (codes CR/CS). This option is only available with the HART 4-20 mA output (code A) [pp. 15, 26, 42, 52, 63, 74]. The standard factory configuration is Alarm = High [p. 109].

MATCH (a:PlantItem {tag: 'P-43-3'}), (b:PlantItem {tag: 'TV-316-2'})
MATCH p = shortestPath((a)-[:line_to*]->(b))
WITH [n IN nodes(p) | n.tag] AS tags
RETURN tags

MATCH (a:PlantItem {tag: 'P-43-3'})
MATCH (a)-[:line_to*1..]->(d:PlantItem)
RETURN DISTINCT d.tag AS tag, d.kind AS kind
ORDER BY tag

MATCH (tv:PlantItem {tag: 'TV-316-2'})
MATCH p = shortestPath((src:PlantItem)-[:line_to*1..]->(tv))
WHERE src.no_inflow = true
RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.tag] AS upstream_path_tags

MATCH (tv:PlantItem {tag: 'TV-316-2'})
OPTIONAL MATCH (up:PlantItem)-[:line_to]->(tv)
OPTIONAL MATCH (tv)-[:line_to]->(down:PlantItem)
RETURN 'upstream' AS direction, up.tag AS tag, up.no_inflow AS no_inflow, up.no_outflow AS no_outflow
UNION
MATCH (tv:PlantItem {tag: 'TV-316-2'})
OPTIONAL MATCH (down:PlantItem)<-[:line_to]-(tv)
RETURN 'downstream' AS direction, down.tag AS tag, down.no_inflow AS no_inflow, down.no_outflow AS no_outflow

MATCH (v:PlantItem {tag: 'TV-316-2'})
OPTIONAL MATCH (u:PlantItem)-[r1:line_to]->(v)
OPTIONAL MATCH (v)-[r2:line_to]->(d:PlantItem)
RETURN CASE WHEN r1 IS NOT NULL THEN u.tag END AS upstream_tag,
       CASE WHEN r2 IS NOT NULL THEN d.tag END AS downstream_tag
ORDER BY upstream_tag, downstream_tag
